{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Joel Alan Appelbaum''' (born December 30, 1941) is an American physicist. 

Appelbaum was born in [[New York City]] on December 30, 1941, and successively earned a Bachelor of Science degree from the [[City University of New York]] in 1963 followed by a Master of Science and PhD in physics at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1964 and 1966, respectively.<ref name="jaaaip">{{cite news |title=J. A. Appelbaum |url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11409012.html |access-date=24 January 2025 |publisher=American Institute of Physics}}</ref> He joined [[Bell Laboratories]] in 1967, taught for one academic year at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], then returned to Bell, where he remained until 1994.<ref name="jaaaip"/><ref name="pt1979"/> While affiliated with Bell Labs, Appelbaum was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1978<ref name="apshonsearch">{{cite news |title=Honors and award winners |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/winners?award_recipients%5Bquery%5D=appelbaum |access-date=24 January 2025 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> and shared the APS [[Davisson-Germer Prize in Atomic or Surface Physics]] with [[Donald R. Hamann]] the following year.<ref name="dgplist">{{cite news |title=Davisson-Germer Prize in Atomic or Surface Physics |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/prize/davisson-germer-prize |access-date=24 January 2025 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref><ref name="pt1979">{{cite journal |title=APS presents six awards at Chicago meeting |journal=Physics Today |date=1979 |volume=32 |issue=4 |pages=69–70 |doi=10.1063/1.2995506}}</ref> Between 1994 and 2000, Appelbaum worked for the [[Micropolis Corporation]].<ref name="jaaaip"/><ref name="ullat"/> He has also worked for [[Univel]].<ref name="ullat">{{cite news |title=Cherokee Shoe in Thousand Oaks said... |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1994-04-19-fi-47660-story.html |access-date=24 January 2025 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=19 April 1994}}</ref>
